sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Cu–Zn binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset CuZn-08Gie.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, (Cu) + L → β, lies at 899 °C.
The Cu–Zn system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as peritectic, intermetallic rich, order disorder.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry (Hallstedt, 2025), which reproduces the assessment of W. Gierlotka, S.-W. Chen, J. Mater. Res., 23, 258-63(2008).
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
The melting point of Cu reproduced by the dataset is 1085 °C.
The melting point of Zn reproduced by the dataset is 420 °C.
We obtain 899 °C for the peritectic reaction ((Cu) + L → β), where L has a mole fraction of 0.375.
Peritectic equilibrium β + L → γ is found at 834 °C and x(Zn) = 0.593 (L).
The peritectic reaction γ + L → δ is calculated at 703 °C, with L at x(Zn) = 0.804.
The dataset places a peritectic (δ + L → ε) at 600 °C; the composition of L is a mole fraction of 0.883.
We obtain 559 °C for the eutectoid reaction (δ → γ + ε), where δ has a mole fraction of 0.749.
The dataset places a peritectoid (β + γ → β′) at 463 °C; the composition of β′ is a mole fraction of 0.491.
The eutectoid reaction β → (Cu) + β′ is calculated at 460 °C, with β at x(Zn) = 0.445.
The dataset places a eutectic (L → ε + (Zn)) at 419 °C; the composition of L is a mole fraction of 0.980.
At 1450 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its minimum, −6.44 kJ/mol, at x(Zn) = 0.440.
The calculated enthalpy of formation of γ at 298.15 K is −10.64 kJ/mol per mole of atoms.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
